judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence insuring agreement whose only flaw is the OCR typo 'THES POLICY', which changes nothing; 'subject to all the terms' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply incorporates the rest of the policy and does not contradict the coverage forms (CP 00 10, CP 00 30) or the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'THIS PREMIUM MAY BE SUBJECT TO ADJUSTMENT' is open-ended but the mechanism is supplied elsewhere; no term is genuinely two-meaninged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Calculation of Premium Endorsement (c029) and the Premium Audit condition (c255) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Insurance at the described premises applies only for the coverages shown below' is a short declarative limit; nothing in it carries two meanings on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is some tension with the blanket limits shown in the Declarations and with A.1 Covered Property (c035), which keys coverage to buildings 'described in the Declarations', but no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single line stating products-completed operations are included subject to the General Aggregate Limit; terse but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section III.3 (c244), which makes a separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate the most payable, and with definition V.16.b.(3) (c275) which resolves the overlap; the fit is awkward but harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard first-named-insured cancellation right; 'advance written notice' leaves the notice period unstated but the effective date is set by the notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated verbatim at c072 and is not disturbed by the Kansas amendatory endorsement IL 02 61 (c185), which replaces only Paragraph 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise two-tier notice schedule (10 days/30 days) with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 02 61 (c185) expressly replaces this paragraph and adds reason-for-cancellation limits, so the printed text and the endorsement point different ways until the replacement rule is applied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Last mailing address known to us' is a settled, workable formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the duplicate at c074 and with the nonrenewal notice provision (c186).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short declarative sentences fixing the end of the policy period; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits consistently with the cancellation and premium-refund paragraphs (c009) and the installment-payment condition (c016).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be less than pro rata' is indefinite about the short-rate calculation, which is a mild vagueness a policyholder could contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision fixes the refund basis, so nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single evidentiary rule with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the identical rule in the nonrenewal endorsement (c186) and the duplicate at c077.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause plus a rule that terms can be amended 'only by endorsement'; the two sentences sit uneasily but each is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is in fact amended by numerous endorsements (IL 02 61, CP 01 01, CP 15 56), which is what this clause contemplates, so there is no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An audit right limited by time; the only defect is OCR mangling of 'We' and 'they'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c079 and consistent with the Premium Audit condition (c255).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The OCR text is badly scrambled and internally refers to 'Paragraphs 1. and 2. of this condition' that no longer appear as numbered, leaving the cross-reference unanchored.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel printing at c080 states the same condition differently (no paragraph numbering, no boiler/elevator carve-out), an internal divergence between two copies of the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates premium responsibility and return-premium payee in two clear numbered items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the duplicate at c081 and with Premium Audit (c255).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anyone having proper temporary custody' is somewhat vague, but it is a familiar and narrow formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the CGL Who Is An Insured provisions (c238 c. and d.) rather than conflicting with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming provision that a court could read against the drafter, and 'date and time of cancelation' is left to the notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It authorises cancellation for a missed installment without expressly honouring the 10-day notice in c006 or the Kansas reason-limits in IL 02 61 (c185), a real fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A truncated applicability heading; there is nothing substantive in it to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fuller version at c084 lists the conditions that apply; the two printings differ only in completeness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void' and 'material fact' are settled insurance terms, though 'material' always invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (c196) replaces this condition for Kansas with a 'we will not pay' formulation rather than avoidance of the whole Coverage Part, so the two provisions point different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Beyond your direction or control' is a familiar limiting phrase; the provision is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 (c190) supersedes and replaces the Control of Property condition for townhouse risks, creating two differently worded versions in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single anti-stacking sentence with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the several Additional Coverages and Extensions declared to be 'additional insurance' (c051, c053), which a court could see as a tension over stacking.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all of the terms' is a strict condition precedent that is routinely litigated, but its words are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A (c187) replaces this condition with a five-year suit limitation for Kansas, so the printed two-year bar contradicts the endorsement left in the same policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any revision that would broaden the coverage' is somewhat open-textured but the operation of the clause is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses mid-term broadening, so no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR has eaten several words ('No person or organization ... having custody'), but the sense is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Personal Property of Others provisions (c035c, c046) which pay only for the owner's account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The division between 'same plan, terms, conditions and provisions' insurance and all other insurance is a classic source of argument about which limb applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the excess wording in the Non-Owned Detached Trailers extension (c050) and the CGL Other Insurance clause (c253) without direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss or damage commencing' during the policy period is precise enough and the territory list is closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c093 and consistent with the described premises in Kansas.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver list ('someone insured', a firm you own or control, 'your tenant') is a closed enumeration whose reach could be argued, and 'to or for whom' differs from the other printing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel printing at c092/c094 says 'to or from whom' and CP 01 01 E (c194) supersedes this condition for Builders' Risk; the same condition therefore appears in two different forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but tightly structured exclusion; each limb is defined by reference to statute and defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that it modifies Liquor Liability and Commercial Auto Coverage Parts that this policy does not contain, an oddity of fit rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The OCR has dropped the operative words of several definitions ('Source material,' 'special nuclear material,' ... Atomic Energy Act), leaving definitions with no verb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined terms are used only in c027, and nothing else in the policy defines them differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain renewal-rating rule with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c092 and consistent with the Declarations' statement that premium may be adjusted (c002).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proportionate part of any policyholder's dividend if declared' is conditional but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other mutual-company conditions (c031, c032); duplicated at c095.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes membership, voting and a specific meeting time and place; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c096 in identical terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-assessment guarantee; the only flaw is the OCR 'labile' for 'liable'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the Calculation of Premium Endorsement (c029) allowing rate recomputation at renewal, but that is prospective, not an assessment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading instruction and pronoun key; purely definitional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to 'Section H. — Definitions' which does exist in this form (c069-c071).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is short and standard; 'direct physical loss of or damage to' is heavily litigated generally but not ambiguous on its face here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties coverage to 'the premises described in the Declarations' while the Declarations write blanket limits across nine locations, a fit question resolved by c053 and the blanket schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long enumerations with the residual 'all other personal property owned by you and used in your business', and the 'if not covered by other insurance' qualifier on additions under construction, invite general-versus-specific argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.3 (c191) adds a further Property Not Covered item and the Declarations' blanket building limit must be read with it; harmonisable but not seamless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long exclusionary list containing genuinely contestable boundaries ('Land (including land on which the property is located)', 'foundations ... below the lowest basement floor', paved surfaces) but each item is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item k. (property more specifically described elsewhere) has to be reconciled with the Other Insurance condition (c024), and c191 adds item q.; the fit is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to the applicable Causes of Loss form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show Special Form and CP 10 30 is attached (c099), so the reference resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very detailed with worked examples; the 180-day reporting condition and the 25% cap are arithmetically defined rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $10,000 additional amount must be squared with Limits Of Insurance (c053), which the provision itself addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If it is necessary to move' and the 30-day window are clear and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly coordinated with Limits Of Insurance (c053), which says preservation payments do not increase the limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capped, two-limb coverage with a stated no-deductible rule; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c053 confirms this limit is in addition to the Limits of Insurance, so the two agree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out for testing 'performed in the course of extracting' is a fine line but the $10,000 annual cap is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the pollutant exclusion (c117) and with Debris Removal's exclusion of pollutant extraction (c038).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blanket-limit formula ('$10,000 or 5% times the value of the damaged building ... times the applicable coinsurance percentage') and the two-year 'as soon as reasonably possible' condition are both genuinely contestable, and e.(8) concedes the wording can 'conflict'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides the Ordinance Or Law Exclusion (c101) and departs from the Loss Payment (c059), Valuation (c063) and Replacement Cost (c067) ordinance-cost exclusions, so the instrument says opposite things about code-upgrade costs depending on where one reads.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and internally defined, with a hard $2,500 annual cap and an express virus carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with Property Not Covered item n. (c036) and the Business Income computer-interruption coverage (c161).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger 'If a Coinsurance percentage of 80% or more or, a Value Reporting period symbol, is shown' is mispunctuated and the 100-foot geographic qualifier is applied inconsistently to the extensions that follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show 100% coinsurance, so the trigger is satisfied; no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Intended for similar use as the building described in the Declarations' is a soft criterion, but the dollar caps and 30-day period are firm.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Business Income newly-acquired-locations extension (c162) and consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Personal effects' is undefined and the theft carve-out applies only to limb (1), a small drafting asymmetry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Personal Property of Others in c035c and the owner's-account rule there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carefully split between additional insurance for lost information and non-additional cost of blank material; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with Property Not Covered item o. (c036) and the Electronic Data coverage (c043).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Temporarily at a location you do not own, lease or operate' is mildly vague as to 'temporarily' but otherwise closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing off-premises provision in the property forms; consistent with c147 Property In Transit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed five-cause list with hard sub-limits; the words themselves are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 D (c193) revises the per-tree figure from $250 to $500, so the printed $250 in this extension is contradicted by an endorsement in the same policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tightly conditioned on contractual responsibility and hitching status; nothing genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its excess-insurance sentence must be read with the Other Insurance condition (c024) but does not contradict it.
